parts.note: a man is someone, any person
to drill soldiers is to train them

explanation.surface: Looking for a person to train some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone to train' reads as a request for a trainer; it is just two pieces, MAN and DRILL, and the animal is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African baboon with a brightly coloured face.

parts.note: bluestockings are learned women, so a Master of Arts degree (MA) plus women (LADIES)
bluestockings are women of learning: the women part gives ladies

explanation.surface: A grumble about the grievances of intellectual women.
explanation.walkthrough: A bluestocking is an old name for a learned woman, read here as MA (a graduate) plus LADIES; 'complaints' in the sense of illnesses is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are illnesses or ailments.

clue.text: Philosopher shows unusual zest in the recess

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the word for a recess

parts.note: a niche is a recess in a wall

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of zest appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A thinker displays odd enthusiasm while tucked into an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest' suggests enthusiasm but is anagram fodder: 'unusual' rearranges it to ETZS, which goes 'in' after the first two letters of the recess word.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was the German thinker behind the idea of the superman.

clue.text: Offend again, that's the substance here

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sin is to offend, as against morals

explanation.surface: A repeat offender pointing to some material.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's pieces come in reverse order: 'Offend' gives SIN, 'again' gives RE, and the answer puts RE first.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky material exuded by trees, used in varnishes.

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: mysterious says the letters of rites are jumbled into a puzzling order

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about to watch strange ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious rites' sounds like occult ritual; 'mysterious' simply rearranges the letters of rites to ITERS, which follow the old word for behold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dawdles or hangs about idly is said to linger.

explanation.surface: A short query about resisting a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest against is to oppose; a thing or article is also called an item, a sense covering both meanings.

parts.note: brand is a poetic word for a sword
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A creature that ends up with a swordfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sword-fish' looks like the single fish with a long bill; the hyphen splits it into a poetic word for a sword and a sea fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: The brandling is a red earthworm with bands, used by anglers as bait.

clue.text: Priest gets me to take up Rousseau's work

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A cleric picks up a famous French book.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI and ME together give ELIME; 'to take up' turns the whole run upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousseau wrote the novel-treatise on education named after its pupil hero, published in 1762.

clue.text: Number in the resort went yearly.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across word breaks

explanation.surface: A tally of how many visited a holiday town each year.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'resorT WENT Yearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is the figure two times ten.

indicators.note: about means the facial word goes around the abbreviation for a work

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An article about a piece by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a newspaper article; it is the chin, which goes 'about' OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was a Polish pianist and writer of mazurkas and nocturnes.

clue.text: Grounds for taking a forger for a former Postmaster-General!

parts.note: lees are the dregs or grounds at the bottom of wine
a smith forges metal, so is a forger

explanation.surface: Evidence of a counterfeiter's guilt against an ex-head of the Post Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter but is the metalworker at the forge. H. B. Lees-Smith ran the British Post Office as Postmaster-General in 1929-31.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings Lees-Smith was a Labour politician who held the cabinet post in charge of the mails.

explanation.surface: A comment on drama and the actors in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: A SIDE is a team, a set of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark an actor makes to the audience unheard by others on stage; a team of players is a side.

clue.text: Number join the same Japanese sect

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again
Zen is a school of Buddhism strong in Japan

explanation.surface: A count of people joining one Buddhist school.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the old abbreviation of ditto, used in lists to mean 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is twelve, a counted quantity.

explanation.surface: Something right for working changing hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift work' suggests factory rotas; 'shift' here means a makeshift device, a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advantageous is fitting; a stopgap or makeshift device is also called by this word.

indicators.note: gathering means the letters of to cress are collected up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sees to the picking of salad leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like harvesting the cress; it rearranges TO CRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany or attend them.

clue.text: In his job he may look for a rise after a fall

definitions.text: In his job he may look for a rise after a fall

parts.words: In his job he may look for a rise after a fall
parts.note: a worker hoping for promotion after a setback, but really someone whose trade is bringing down showers, after which crops grow

explanation.surface: A worker hoping for promotion after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fall' is of rain and the 'rise' is crops springing up after it; the clue reads like a career comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal or folk figure who claims to bring showers by magic in times of drought.

explanation.surface: Gossip spreading round the island of The Tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, Caliban says the isle is full of these 'sounds and sweet airs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmurs or talk can be called this; the island where Caliban lives is full of sounds of music.

clue.text: Have in mind to do a good turn, perhaps ?

definitions.text: to do a good turn, perhaps

explanation.surface: Thinking of performing a kind act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good turn' suggests a kindness; here a turn is a stage act, so doing one amuses an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour an idea is to consider it; a performer doing a stage act amuses people.

clue.text: Those who stove in these casks

explanation.surface: The people who smashed these barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stove in' is the past tense of stave in, meaning smashed. Small water casks on boats are also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: People who smashed things; small water barrels carried on a ship's lifeboat.

clue.text: Negligent sapper has a bad shot

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
a miss is a shot that fails to hit

explanation.surface: A careless army engineer fires wide.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, RE, in British army slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless or neglectful of duty.

clue.text: Sign of promotion in the band

explanation.surface: Rank badge in the regimental music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians; it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron on a sleeve marks a rise in rank; a strip or line of colour is also so called.

explanation.surface: A boat that sparks a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships; also a device for kindling a cigarette.

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, stands for a pound
a currency that appreciates is worth more

explanation.surface: Sterling gains value across the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound appreciates' looks like currency news; L (pound) plus IS MORE. The definition is a place 'in Ireland'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lismore is a town in County Waterford with a well-known castle.

explanation.surface: Lots of joblessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for loose trousers, the first meaning; slack times are periods with little work.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual trousers were once called bags; quiet spells with no work are slack periods.

clue.text: Settle the money for the guides

parts.note: to land is to come to rest or settle
marks were German money

explanation.surface: Pay the cash to the tour leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle the money' reads as paying up; it is LAND (settle) plus MARKS, the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent features that help travellers find their way serve as guides.

clue.text: Some fine athletic types in Glamorganshire

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few sporty people from South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'types', but the place is defined by 'in Glamorganshire' alone; 'types' completes the phrase holding fiNE ATHletic. Neath is a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in the former Welsh county of Glamorgan.

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

indicators.note: back means the word for look is read from right to left

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A young woman makes an academic glance behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look back' reads as glancing behind; 'back' turns the word for an appearance into RIA, after the degree abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a female given name.

indicators.note: carrying means the word for food holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: opener picks out the first letter of the word tin

explanation.surface: A road builder eats, holding a can opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' looks like a kitchen tool; it is T, the opening letter of 'tin', carried inside MEAL. Road metal is broken stone for making roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone used for building road surfaces is called road metal.

explanation.surface: Rotate the obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle turned to work a machine; also an eccentric with a fixed enthusiasm.

indicators.note: about means the word for writing goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

indicators.note: making says the letters of tart are made into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe writer inclined to bake pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' turns TART into TRAT, which PROSE goes 'about'. 'Prone to' looks like 'inclined to', but 'Prone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat face downwards.

clue.text: A painter has retired—-that's a waste !

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the whole run reads in reverse

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: An artist has given up: it was all wasted effort.
explanation.walkthrough: A RA HAS read backwards. 'waste' suggests futility; here it is a desert waste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is a vast desert, a wilderness or waste of sand.

explanation.surface: Turns down the chance to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To say no to an offer; to sink or diminish.
